title: Kubernetes Audit Log Baseline

controlTest.positiveScenario: Replay or inject sample `kube:audit` events matching `*` into `index=kube`. Confirm UC-4.9.1 search returns >=1 row and alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign `kube:audit` traffic without `*` markers. Confirm the search returns zero rows and alert does not fire.

description: Verifies kubernetes audit log baseline data flows into Splunk continuously.
value: Kubernetes Audit Log Baseline is the prerequisite feed for all 4.9 detections.
implementation: Enable kube:audit ingestion via the appropriate Splunk TA into index=kube.
visualization: Ingestion health single value and lag chart.
knownFalsePositives: Approved change windows; documented automation service principals; sandbox accounts excluded via lookup.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with permission to search `index=kube`.
• Install and configure: Splunk Connect for Kubernetes (Splunkbase 4467).
• Ensure `kube:audit` events are flowing (prerequisite UC: none when applicable).
• Map `kube` and field extractions per `docs/guides/aws.md`, `docs/guides/azure.md`, or `docs/guides/gcp.md` as appropriate.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Enable kube:audit ingestion via the appropriate Splunk TA into index=kube.
Expected sourcetype: `kube:audit`. Validate with:
```spl
index=kube sourcetype="kube:audit" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=kube sourcetype="kube:audit"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress errorCode
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
The search scopes `kube:audit` in `index=kube` and applies `*` to surface `Kubernetes Audit Log Baseline`. Tune time range and alert threshold to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare result counts to the vendor console (CloudTrail Event history, Azure Activity Log, GCP Logs Explorer, or service-native UI). Spot-check `_time` and actor fields. Confirm CIM acceleration only after TA field mappings are verified.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_9_1_alert` with appropriate severity. Dashboard: Ingestion health single value and lag chart..
Failure modes: (1) empty results — verify TA input and index routing; (2) duplicate events — check S3/SQS duplication; (3) missing fields — upgrade `Splunk Connect for Kubernetes (Splunkbase 4467)` and review `props.conf` aliases; (4) alert fatigue — add CMDB/allow-list exclusions documented in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch for kubernetes audit log baseline in your cloud audit logs so the team catches important changes early instead of finding out from auditors or customers.
